doc.title: Bobby Shew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 1, 2020

title: Woody Herman, Si Zentner, Terry Gibbs and Buddy Rich as bosses
summary: Shew compares other leaders, and tells of Buddy Rich's remark through his wife that he could never replace Shew.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Oh you should know him. That’s his mom. She’s his mom. Matt is a brilliant young saxophone player. He lives in Vegas, and a writer and all of that. He was on Louie Bellson’s band and all of that. Anyway, so Benny was the worst of them. You know Woody Herman was cool except that Woody could be really icy cold at times you know, and you know I’ve seen him downgrade Sal Nestico when we were on the band together. And Nat Pierce wrote a ballad for Sal, “Easy Living” I think it was, and Woody wouldn’t let him play it. He wanted Sal to always do that fast [scats] machine gun stuff. And Sal wanted to play a ballad and Woody wouldn’t let him you know. Woody was like, he could be cruel. You know. But then one of the nicest guys I ever worked for was Si Zentner actually you know. Just a general warm guy, friendly, cool, positive, encouraging at all times. Terry Gibbs was a lot of fun to work for you know. Terry had a few quirks here and there once in a while that you know he would get a hair up his butt and scream about something that was totally not worth screaming about you know. But you know, and then the other guy that I — Buddy Rich of course, who I worked for, was one of the greatest experiences musically that I ever had but one of the most intense emotional kind of nervous kind of things. Well you know the stories about Buddy you know, and talk about bipolar, there’s another one too you know. And you know Buddy was like, Buddy and I he loved me, and the greatest compliment that I ever got in my entire career came indirectly from Buddy, through his wife. My wife and Marie Rich were good friends before I met my wife actually. Because my wife was a dancer in Vegas and she used to dance in a show opposite the Harry James band when Buddy was on Harry’s band. And so we used to, after I left Buddy’s band, Marie and my wife and I we used to go out and go to dinner sometimes together. And so the story that Marie said to me, she said, “Buddy was on a break and he was home and she came to him in the living room and said ‘Oh I saw Bobby and Lisa Shew today, and they said to say hello to you.’” And Buddy did the four letter word Bobby Shew you know. And she said, “Why do you hate him so
much?” He said, “Because I’ve never been able to replace him.” And she told me that and I went — wow you couldn’t pat me on the back any further than that you know. What a compliment from Buddy.
Indeed. Those were some great records.

That was years after I had left the band. And he had probably gone through another ten lead players trying to find one. But see I grew up playing drums when I was 14 and so Buddy could hear something about me knowing the drums in my playing.
